newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to tax T-bill earnings at 15 pct.
newsitem.headline: Russia to tax T-bill earnings at 15 pct.

text.p: Russia's Justice Ministry has approved a request by the Finance Ministry to treat earnings from the discount on GKO Treasury bills as interest, which qualifies for a 15 percent tax rate, a senior Finance Ministry official said on Tuesday.

"According to the instruction, both accrued earnings on GKOs, arising from primary placement and earnings arising from secondary market trading will be subject to tax at a rate of 15 percent," said Bella Zlatkis, head of the Finance Ministry's securities department.
The Justice Ministry's ruling backs the Finance Ministry's interpretation of a new tax on government securities.
That set a 15 percent for interest paid on bond coupons, but implied that the usual profit tax rates of 35-43 percent had been extended to other earnings on government paper.

The wording of the law introducing the tax had not made it clear whether earnings from the discount on T-bills were to be treated as interest, which had been the Finance Ministry's intention, or as general profits.
As a result the Finance Ministry and Federal Tax Service drafted instructions interpreting the law which they submitted to the Justice Ministry for approval.

The new tax applies only to new securities issued after the tax came into force last month. Because of the uncertainty the Finance Ministry has been issuing for the last couple of weeks only additional tranches of older issues which are not subject to the tax.
